name: Lying Face
baseMeaning: A yellow face with a long nose like Pinocchio, indicating a lie or fib.
tldr: 🤥 marks a fib, calls out a doubtful claim, or jokingly admits that something untrue was said.

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤥 directly says that a statement or story is false.
🤥 works as a skeptical reaction to an obvious exaggeration or unlikely excuse.
contextMeanings.example: you stayed up until 3 watching one episode 🤥

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤥 jokingly admits that the sender is the person who lied.
contextMeanings.example: i only checked my phone once during the movie 🤥

contextMeanings.meaning: 🤥 can express frustration by implying that an explanation is false or evasive.
contextMeanings.example: great, another ‘quick’ update. nothing changed at all 🤥

platformNotes.note: In comments, 🤥 often accompanies an exaggerated story as a playful challenge: “you really woke up at 5 for that coffee?” It can also mark a creator’s obvious acting when the caption already makes the joke.

On Twitter, a lone 🤥 tends to function as a blunt reaction to a boast, suspicious claim, or contradiction. The short format leaves the target open, so nearby words often determine whether it feels teasing or accusatory.

In Instagram messages, 🤥 is common in playful exchanges about late replies, pretend excuses, or overstated plans. Sending it between photos usually adds teasing skepticism rather than demanding a literal confession.

In Slack, 🤥 can label a colleague’s convenient explanation without requiring a long dispute. Outside close work groups, though, the same emoji may sound more pointed because the surrounding relationship is less visible.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z often uses 🤥 as a joke about an obvious lie, especially when the truth is already clear from context. It can function like a teasing “caught you,” although serious accusations still use it.

Millennials tend to read 🤥 straightforwardly as “that is not true,” with jokes and sarcasm determining how aggressively it lands. In a familiar group chat, it may simply invite the sender to explain the story.
Gen X recipients may take 🤥 more literally, particularly when the sender is someone they do not know well. The emoji’s accusation can feel less playful there, especially in a serious disagreement.

warnings.title: Teasing becomes an accusation
warnings.description: A recipient may hear “you are lying” rather than “that sounds unlikely,” especially if the relationship is new. Pair the emoji with a light question or use 😅 when the concern is genuinely mild.

warnings.title: The joke obscures the real problem
warnings.description: 🤥 can make a complaint sound like banter when someone needs a straight answer. State the discrepancy plainly, or ask for clarification instead of relying on the emoji to carry the criticism.

seoDescription: What does 🤥 mean? It marks a playful fib, calls out a claim that is untrue, or adds skeptical humor to an exaggerated story.

longForm.overview:
🤥 is built around a simple visual joke: the yellow face has a long Pinocchio-style nose, so the emoji points directly at a false statement. Added in Unicode 9.0, it began with an unusually clear job—marking a lie, fib, or claim the sender does not believe.

That clear job does not make every use a serious accusation. 🤥 can be a teasing “nice try,” an ironic acknowledgment that the sender is the one lying, or a skeptical marker attached to an obviously exaggerated story. Its meaning changes with the sentence, relationship, and delivery. A friend who writes “i said i’d only buy one, but… 🤥” is joking about their own bad decision; a colleague who writes “the report was accurate 🤥” may be challenging the report. What people get wrong is treating the long nose as proof that 🤥 always means “you are lying.” It can also be the punchline itself.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
People usually reach for 🤥 when a claim is so exaggerated that the emoji can deliver the disbelief for them. It often follows a boast, an implausible excuse, a contradicted alibi, or a story whose details do not quite fit. The emoji also appears when someone admits their own minor dishonesty: “i was going to eat just one, but… 🤥.”

The surrounding text determines the force. “You watched the whole finale without falling asleep? 🤥” sounds teasing, while “that never happened 🤥” directly rejects the claim. In group chats, 🤥 can stand alone as a reaction when everyone already understands the joke. It may also point out that someone’s stated reason does not match what happened, making it useful for calling out a dodge without writing a stern paragraph.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 🤥 when the issue needs a precise answer rather than a comic reaction. If money, work, loyalty, or a health matter is involved, the long-nose joke can distract from the actual problem. Say exactly what is inaccurate and ask for an explanation; a neutral question like “what happened?” keeps the conversation from turning into a contest over who gets to lie.

Older recipients or people who know you less well may also take the emoji literally. A joke about missed plans can sound like an accusation, and a playful 🤥 aimed at a relative may create unnecessary tension. Use 😅, 🙃, or plain wording when the point is mild. If someone is discussing grief, illness, or another painful subject, leave the emoji out entirely.
longForm.howToReply:
If 🤥 arrives as playful skepticism, match its energy with a brief explanation, a wink, or another 🤥. For example, “okay, the video was only two hours” can continue the joke without treating it as a serious challenge. To escalate, ask a specific question: “wait, what time did you actually leave?” That moves the exchange toward the story instead of repeating the accusation.

If 🤥 lands on something you shared and feels harsher than intended, respond plainly: “that part was exaggerated, but the rest was true.” If you sent it and the other person seems confused, clarify whether you were teasing or genuinely disputing their claim. A quick explanation preserves the joke while making the actual level of seriousness clear.

faqs.question: What does 🤥 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: 🤥 has no gender-specific meaning. It usually says that he thinks a claim is false, is teasing you about an obvious exaggeration, or is jokingly admitting his own lie.

faqs.question: Is 🤥 flirty?
faqs.answer: 🤥 is not inherently flirty; it normally points to dishonesty or disbelief. It can appear in playful flirting when the joke involves a shared excuse, but the surrounding words determine that meaning.

faqs.question: What does 🤥 mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: On TikTok, 🤥 commonly reacts to an exaggerated story, suspicious excuse, or obvious boast. It is often playful when the creator has already invited disbelief through the joke itself.

faqs.question: Can 🤥 be serious?
faqs.answer: Yes. When attached to a disputed fact, 🤥 can mean “that is false” and may open a serious confrontation. Use plain language if the distinction between a fib and a consequential lie matters.

conversationExamples.message: i only ate two of the pizza rolls 🤥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is jokingly confessing to eating more than they admitted. Reply with “sure you did” or ask how many are actually left.

conversationExamples.message: my flight was delayed six hours and i still made it on time 🤥
conversationExamples.interpretation: This marks the story as an obvious exaggeration or boast. The sender probably wants the audience to call out the implausible timing.

conversationExamples.message: he said he was at the office all night, then posted stories from the bar 🤥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji highlights the contradiction and suggests distrust. A good reply asks what happened rather than accusing him outright.

conversationExamples.message: the invoice went out friday, but it’s still sitting in drafts 🤥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is calmly pointing out that the stated action did not happen. Respond by checking the actual status and correcting the record.

conversationExamples.message: i only put one plate of cookies out 🤥
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is teasing themselves or another family member about disappearing cookies. Reply with a playful accusation about how many they actually ate.
